newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian royalists hold rival in simmering spat.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian royalists hold rival in simmering spat.

text.p: Cambodian royalists in the country's northwest are holding an official of a rival party in retaliation for the arrest of two of their own members, sources from both sides said on Monday.

"Yesterday (Sunday) we arrested a Cambodian People's Party commune chief from Moung district and he is being looked after well...We consider him a political prisoner," said senior police officer Vorn Chhunly of the royalist FUNCINPEC party.
FUNCINPEC and the Cambodian People's Party (CPP) are joined in an uneasy coalition government set up after U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993.
Differences have been exacerbated by the defection of thousands of Khmer Rouge guerrillas to the government side.

The officer, contacted by telephone in the northwest province of Battambang, said he was ready to release the unidentified provincial official once the CPP released two FUNCINPEC security personnel alleged to have been detained in the province on January 17.
Deputy police chief Mek Dara of the CPP, also contacted in Battambang, confirmed that FUNCINPEC police had arrested the commune chief while he was riding home on a motorbike.

Relations between Battambang Governor Ung Samy of the CPP and his deputy Serei Kosal of FUNCINPEC plummeted in November after clashes between the two parties in the province left several people wounded.
The two were told to cooperate in holding local and general elections due by the end of 1998, but ill-feeling has continued to simmer amid fresh reports of violence and intimidation.
